note: Lightbulb shaped CME occurring in association with a filament eruption seen to the north in SOHO LASCO C2 and north-northeast in STEREO A COR2 occurring near the vicinity of Active Region 14000 (N18E20) seen best in GOES SUVI 304 and SDO AIA 304. It expands significantly in later imagery, particularly SOHO C3 imagery, becoming much more wide.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using all available imagery from two spacecraft out to approximately 18 solar radii.

note: Fairly slow CME seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and farther south in STEREO A COR2A; the source is possibly associated with a filament eruption seen in SDO AIA 304 occurring on the Earth-facing disk around 2025-02-21T06:30Z, however, the CME appears to fit to a longitude of W30 to W50 which is not associated with any eruptions visible on the Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft measurement of the leading edge using triangulation of the leading edge to determine the longitude.

note: The first in a series of three overlapping CMEs. This CME is visible to the W/slightly NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and similarly to the W/slightly NW in STEREO A COR2. The leading edge is more faint and narrow than those of the other subsequent CMEs. The source of this CME is part of a complex eruption taking place on the NW limb in SDO imagery. As early as 2025-02-20T18:00Z in SDO AIA 193, a loop over the NW limb can be seen beginning to slowly rise, located above or near some destabilizing filament material hovering above on the NW limb in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 as well as general location of the complex candidate source.

note: The second in a series of three overlapping CMEs. This CME is visible to the W/slightly NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and similarly to the W/slightly NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is part of a complex eruption taking place on the NW limb in SDO imagery. At 2025-02-21T09:24Z, a wide loop snaps open in SDO AIA 171/193, and some filamentary material rapidly rises high in the corona but fails to escape solar gravitational forces, remaining suspended in the corona for a few hours. The wide loop that snapped open is a candidate source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 as well as location of the complex candidate source.

note: The third in a series of three overlapping CMEs. This bright flux rope CME is visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is part of a complex eruption taking place on the NW limb in SDO imagery. Around 2025-02-21T11:27Z, suspended filament material finally ejects outward in SDO AIA 171/193/304. A large post-eruptive arcade on the NW limb also begins around 2025-02-21T11:27Z, expanding from N10->N35 on/just inside the NW limb. This filament eruption is also visible in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery, showing post-eruptive arcades and brightening stretching from N35W60 to N15W90, near AR 3989 (~N20W85) [30 degrees have been added to all STEREO A EUVI longitudes to translate to Earth-facing disk coordinates].

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 as well as the location of the source filament eruption as seen in available UV imagery of the disk.

note: Slow, narrow and faint CME to the southwest, mostly seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. No source has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: No source has been found for this CME and it is completely covered by a data gap in STEREO A imagery, so only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

note: Faint, wide, multi-front streamer blowout CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. A data gap in STEREO A COR2 from 2025-02-21T15:53Z to 2025-02-22T03:23Z completely covers this CME. The source is not discernable on the Earth-facing disk and is likely farsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. Tricky to track the same leading edge between C2 and C3, since there are several slow loops that emerge in C2 and eventually merge into one brighter loop by the time C3's field of view is reached. There is also a data gap in STEREO A COR2 from 2025-02-21T15:53Z to 2025-02-22T03:23Z which completely covers this CME.

note: A loop CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO but partially obscured by pylon in C3 and covered by the 202-02-21T15:53Z-2025-02-22T03:23Z gap in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a minor activity close to the NW limb (possibly in AR 3989 located at N19W90 at the time on in AR 4001 that is also close to the NW limb), manifesting as the opening/movement of field lines on/close to the NW limb that is seen in SDO AIA 193/171 and GOES SUVI 284 EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate one-coronagraph (SOHO LASCO) coronagraph analysis based on the very approximate/uncertain source location (minor activity on/near the NW limb).

note: A very faint narrow outflow/front, faintly seen in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2, with no clear source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, in the absence of clear source.

note: A fuzzy front seen in SOHO LASCO C2, but covered by the pylon in C3. The source is likely the C8.3 flare from AR 4001 (N24W76) peaking at 2025-02-22T21:07Z, and an associated very minor dimming/post eruptive arcades seen in AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 at the time.

cmeAnalyses.note: One-coronagraph analysis (with SOHO LASCO), based on the location of the likely source (associated flare).

note: A fuzzy front to the southwest seen in SOHO LASCO. The source could be a narrow opening of field lines on/behind the SW limb seen in AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky analysis made while there is no STEREO A imagery.

note: CME seen to the northwest associated with an M4.9-class flare from AR 14001 which peaked at 2025-02-23T02:13Z at N25W82. Beginning around 2025-02-23T02:09Z, wide opening field lines and small post-eruptive arcades are observed in SDO AIA 171/193. First of three CMEs emanating from this area including the faster 02:48Z CME and slower/outflow-related 03:24Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge/bulk measurement fit to the source using two spacecraft, despite STEREO A imagery being in a campaign and limiting available imagery.

note: Very fast and thin CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 out ahead of the 2025-02-23T03:24Z CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery; the source is likely associated with an M4.9-class flare from AR 4001 which peaked at 2025-02-23T02:13Z at N25W82 (14001). Beginning around 2025-02-23T02:09Z, wide opening field lines and small post-eruptive arcade are seen in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the leading edge using only SOHO C2/C3; inclusion of STEREO A COR2A data suggests the eruption originates from W55-65 but is not supported by EUV imagery. Uncertainty in longitude about 25 degrees.

note: Likely outflow associated with CME: 2025-02-23T02:36Z, an eruption associated with an M4.9-class flare from AR 14001 which peaked at 2025-02-23T02:13Z at N25W82. Beginning around 2025-02-23T02:09Z, wide opening field lines and small post-eruptive arcade are observed in SDO AIA 171/193. Triangulation with STEREO Ahead suggests the eruption is sourced around W55 but this is not supported by EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: One spacecraft measurement of the leading edge (SOHO), as triangulation of the leading edge with STEREO A seemed to suggest the source region was centered around W55-W65, which is not supported by EUV imagery.

note: Narrow jet CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2; the source may be loose field line movement over AR 4004 (S15E65 at this time) starting around 2025-02-23T10:15Z in SDO AIA 193 but confidence is low.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement of the leading edge before it fades out of SOHO C2.

note: Very wide CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 during a STEREO A COR2A data gap composed with a well-defined western and southwestern leading edge and not-as-defined northern leading edge, associated with an X2.0-class flare and subsequent eruption from AR 14001 (N25W87) as evidenced by strong brightening in SDO AIA 131 and quickly separating field lines seen in SDO AIA 193, 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Shock front measurement using only SOHO imagery, encompassing the entire width of the CME in support of solar energetic particle modeling efforts. WSA-Enlil+CONE simulations associated with this measurement are created in support of solar energetic particle modeling purposes and model outputs should not be used for CME trajectory analysis.

Bulk for trajectory analysis using only SOHO imagery focusing on mid-point of the leading edge in the northwest, the northern portion is faster than this measurement and eastern portion (portion representing the ecliptic plane) is slower than this measurement, due to the tilt of CME out of the ecliptic with respect to occulting disk.

note: Very faint CME to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. Not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be moving/opening field lines along the southern limb as seen in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2025-02-24T00:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky parameters based on best fit using swpc_cat measuring technique and SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery.

note: Bright, wide CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. Source is seen in SDO AIA 171/193/211 as field line movement beginning around 2025-02-24T04:09Z over the NW limb, with an EUV wave at 2025-02-24T05:18Z, and as a filament liftoff starting around 2025-02-24T05:06Z. The source is better seen in STEREO A EUVI with the filament on/just inside the west limb as viewed from STEREO A. At 2025-02-24T05:15Z, STEREO A was located 30.297 degrees from Earth, putting its west limb around W120.3. Here in STEREO A EUVI 304, the filament can be seen slowly rising starting at 2025-02-24T03:15Z->T5:15Z, and ejecting by the next timestamp at T05:45Z. A post-eruptive arcade follows in STEREO A EUVI 195/304. The source could be, or be near, old AR 3989, which rotated off the west limb on 2025-02-21 and would be located approximately W115-W125.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK. Triangulated measurement of the brightest bulk portion of the leading edge, notably clipping some of the more faint nose off the northern portion in SOHO C3 imagery due to the uneven front. This analysis may be preliminary as further analysis continues.

note: CME first seen to the WNW is SOHO LASCO C2. CME is also seen as a partial halo mostly to the NW in STEREO A COR2 but is obscured by the pylon is SOHO LASCO C3. This CME is very difficult to distinguish from the previous CME in white light imagery. The source is most likely associated with an M3.3 flare from AR 14000 (N17W21) that peaked at 2025-02-24T07:02Z. The flare and a region of dimming projected south of the flare are seen across SDO AIA and GOES SUVI wavelengths but are best seen in SDO AIA 193. There also appears to be some western deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on running difference imagery from STEREO A COR2 and on-disk source location. There is significant uncertainty in this measurement due to the lack of measurable LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This CME is very difficult to distinguish from the previous CME is C2 and is obscured by the pylon in C3.

note: Faint CME seen to the NNW in only SOHO LASCO C2, it fades quickly in the FOV after its initial visibility from the occulting disk. No source is observed for this front in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky in SOHO LASCO C2 only as it fades in the FOV.

note: This CME is first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3, but not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2025-02-24T20:23Z. The source of this CME is likely associated with an eruption visible beyond the SW limb starting around 2025-02-24T20:27Z as seen in SDO/AIA 131 with associated brightening, moving/opening field lines, and an EUV wave best seen in SDO/AIA 211. Following the eruption, there were very notably post-eruptive arcades which were associated with a long duration, occulted M3.9 flare from former AR 13990 (S13W120) that peaked at 2024-02-24T23:02Z. The very beginning of the flare can be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 on the W limb in the last frame (2025-02-24T20:35Z) prior to the end of a downlink period. Additionally, very fast opening field lines are visible from beyond the W limb starting around 2025-02-24T20:24Z in SDO/AIA 193, SDO/AIA 171, GOES SUVI 195, and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: This is a SHOCK measurement. Parameters based on best fit adjusted from source location using single-spacecraft measurement method. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap.

This is an updated BULK measurement with later frames. Parameters are based on the best fit of CME features based on potential source location using single-spacecraft measurement method. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap.
Measurement based best fit in running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and probable source location of M3.3 occulted flare from beyond the W limb.

note: Bright CME first seen in the SW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-02-25T12:38Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in later frames. The beginning frames of this event in SOHO LASCO are obscured by a data gap from 25/11:12Z to 25/13:39Z. The source of this CME is an M3.6 flare from AR 3998 (S15W55) as seen in SDO AIA 131. Opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 94, 171 and 193, along with an area of dimming seen in SDO AIA 94, 193, 211 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2

note: Faint CME to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only, missed in STEREO COR2A due to a data gap. The CME travels into the pylon in C3 hindering visibility in white light and running difference imagery. The source is observed as a field line loop breaking over the NW limb around 2025-02-25T14:18Z in SDO AIA 171/193, potentially from old AR 4001 which rotated over the NW limb on 2025-02-24.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only plane-of-sky due to far-sided source with no STEREO COR2A imagery to triangulate with.

note: CME first seen in the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-02-26T06:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. S10W25 exhibiting a strong Westward deflection. This filament is visible in SDO AIA and STEREO A EUVI 304, along with dimming and post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 94, 193 and STEREO A EUVI 195. A large North-South configured coronal hole is visible approximately 10 degrees to the East of the eruptive source. This coronal hole may cause deflection or acceleration of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location. CME is too faint to be reliably tracked and triangulated in STEREO A COR2.

note: Very faint CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-02-26T09:36Z. This event fades before exiting the FOV in C2, and is therefore not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 or STEREO A COR2. There is no clear source seen on the disk for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: POS measurement due to uncertain source location and lack of reliable STEREO A COR2 imagery for triangulation.

note: Bright CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and after a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption seen near S30W70 in SDO/AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-02-26T14:00Z. There is strong southern deflection of the eruption, likely due to the large coronal holes to the north and east of the source location. Field line opening is also visible in SDO/AIA 171, 193, and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of brightest leading edge and bulk of CME.

note: Faint CME visible to the W/SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in a few frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery before a data gap beginning around 2025-02-26T19:00Z. The exact start time of this CME is unclear due to the overlap with the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2025-02-26T15:00Z. The possible source of this CME is a filament eruption beginning around 2025-02-26T11:15Z in STEREO A EUVI, GOES SUVI, and SDO/AIA 304 imagery near ~S15W90+. A slow rising loop is visible in GOES SUVI 304 and 284 imagery along the W/SW limb starting around 2025-02-26T12:00Z which may have been fully released from the lower/middle corona when the filament eruption associated with the overlapping CME to the SW occurred.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in limited imagery in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The CME exhibits an initial faint, diffuse front with a brighter portion (more clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery) that appears to be the bulk of the CME. The source appears to be a possible filament eruption stretching along the eastern side of the large N-S oriented coronal hole located near central meridian. Brightening is visible in SDO/AIA and GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-02-26T14:16Z. Associated dimming and post-eruptive arcades are visible in SDO/AIA 195 and GOES SUVI 284. Deflection is likely for this CME due to the large coronal holes to the west of the source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters are based off of the best fit of the features in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the west/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not observable in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely related to a C3.5 flare and eruption from Active Region 13996 (S16W86) starting around 2025-02-26T22:50Z as seen in SDO AIA 131 imagery. Faint field line movement is visible over the southwest limb at this time in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. It is also visible in SOHO LASCO C2 following a data gap ending at 2025-02-27T07:48Z. The source is likely related to an eruption from Active Region 13996 (S16W89) starting around 2025-02-27T05:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131 and 304 imagery. Faint field line movement is visible over the southwest limb around this time in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Very faint and wide loop CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 and seen after a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2. The leading edge is nearly fully obstructed by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. Source is likely opening loops and field line movement seen just beyond the (STEREO A) northwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery, starting around 2025-02-27T06:25Z and located at about N20W120 (Earth-facing disk coordinates).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using a very limited number of frames. Parameters based on candidate source location seen in STEREO A EUV imagery and best fit between two frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery. There is a data gap that begins in STEREO A COR2 at 2025-02-27T07:53Z and the leading edge is too diffuse to track after the gap ends at 2025-02-27T09:23Z. The leading edge becomes visible halfway through C2 field of view after the end of a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2, and once it enters the C3 field of view, it is almost entirely blocked by the pylon and cannot reliably be tracked.

note: CME visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely Active Region 13996 (S16W90), with an eruption seen starting around 2025-02-27T11:05Z in STEREO A EUVI 195 and SDO AIA 193 imagery. Brightening and dimming are seen from the region, and opening field lines are best seen in SDO AIA 171/193/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-02-27T15:23Z. The source is a filament eruption, with liftoff starting around 2025-02-27T17:36Z, centered around approximately N20E80 as seen in SDO AIA 304. Moving/opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171/193 and dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT. STEREO A COR2 imagery was not available for this measurement.

note: CME first seen the the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-02-28T08:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is field line opening seen just beyond the SW limb in SDO AIA 193. This may be related to activity from AR 3996 (S16W100) which rotated off of the Earth facing disk on 2025-02-27.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen in the NE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-02-28T15:23Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a data gap from 28/14:48Z to 28/16:24Z. The source of this event is a jet-like eruption from Active Region 4006 (N18W02), exhibiting a very strong Northeastern deflection in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Bright, partial halo to halo CME visible in the W/NW of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a far-sided filament eruption visible along the NW limb of STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 starting around 2025-02-28T16:45Z. Post eruptive arcades are also visible in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 starting around 2025-02-28T17:35Z. Moving/opening field lines and an EUV wave is visible in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2025-02-28T17:00Z. The source is suspected to be from AR 13993 (~N15W125) based on available STEREO A EUVI data. Note that there was a simultaneous, much less significant, eruption centered at (~W01W60) at the time of the far-sided eruption associated with this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on the best fit of the BULK of the CME. The leading edge has a slight dimpled shape in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Very approximate analysis of a faint wider shock mostly seen in coronagraph running difference imagery, which seems to be more farsided. This is also confirmed by the fact that the EUV wave is not seen on the Earth facing side in EUV imagery, but there are signatures of a far-sided EUV wave behind the limb, seen in AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

note: CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-02-28T16:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a C5.2 flare and jet-like eruption from Active Region 4006 (N18W02), exhibiting a very strong Northeastern deflection in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. This CME partially overlaps and is obscured by CME: 2025-02-28T17:12Z in later frames.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow CME seen to the north in SOHO LASCO C2 with fainter loops following shortly behind. Associated with a point source eruption from near AR 4006 (N18W10) starting at 2025-03-01T09:18Z with very strong deflection north out of the ecliptic as evidenced by dark filamentary material jetting north in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using two spacecraft indicating strong northern deflection (out of the ecliptic). Uncertainty in latitude about +/- 10 degrees, though the longitude is well confined.

note: This CME is visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery with a very bright core mostly on the right side of the CME. The source is a large L-shaped filament eruption stretching from ~S35W10 to ~S15E40 centered around ~S35E20 starting around 2025-03-01T17:00Z. Brightening is visible in SDO/AIA, GOES SUVI, and STEREO A EUVI 304. Dimming, moving/opening field lines, and post-eruptive arcades are best visible in GOES SUVI 284 and SDO/AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit adjusted from source location with apparent deflection to the south taken into account.

note: This CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery to the S/SE in the outflow of the previous CME starting at 2025-03-01T18:24Z. It is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap beginning at 2025-03-01T21:38Z. The source of this CME is a partially occulted C9.5 flare from a region just beyond the SE limb near S26E90+ as seen in SDO/AIA and GOES SUVI 131 imagery. A well defined loop with filament ejecta in the middle is seen lifting from the source region with clear moving/opening field lines and EUV wave to the south starting around 2025-03-01T23:00Z. There appears to be strong deflection to the south with this event as evident by the moving/opening field lines in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very preliminary measurement with limited frames in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. No STEREO A COR2 available due to data gap. The CME exhibits a sheered-type of front with a portion moving faster than other portions. These parameters are based on following the faster portion of the CME with including the slower portion within the width of the measurement. The slower portion of this CME was measuring speeds closer to 200 km/s.

note: Narrow faint jet to the southeast in both coronagraphs, best seen in running difference imagery. Its source is likely a C2.4 class flare (and a super minor ejecta seen in GOES SUVI 304) from AR 4011 (S18E58) starting at 2025-03-02T03:37Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs. It's somewhat confirmed by the location of the flare (but there seems to be some deflection westward).

note: Faintest of the 3 consecutive narrow jets from AR 4011 this morning. Its source is likely the C1.2 flare from AR 4011 (S18E57) starting at 2025-03-02T05:46Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the location of the likely source (C class flare).

note: Faint narrow CME to the southeast in both coronagraphs, best seen in running difference imagery.  Its source is likely the C2.7 flare and a minor eruption in AR 4011 (S18E54) seen in SDO AIA 131, 304 and GOES SUVI 304, 284 and on SE limb in EUVI A 195 at 2025-03-02T09:57Z. Note that there also seems to be an even more minor eruption off the SW limb at the same time seen in SDO AIA 304/ GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs confirmed by the location of the most likely source - the associated flare.

note: Bright heart-shaped CME to the northwest in both coronagraphs. No source has been found on the Earth-facing disk, but there is a faint flicker/movement of field lines far behind the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 seen most clearly at 2025-03-02T11:09Z but really faintly seen as early as 2025-03-02T10:15Z, and also possibly seen as a faint/indistinct movement beyond the northwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 at 2025-03-02T10:35Z. Most likely this is a backsided CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs. Faint coronal signatures also indicate that this is a far-sided CME.

note: Faint loop only seen in COR2A running difference imagery and overlapping with the earlier more significant 2025-03-02T10:24Z CME; this event is not clearly seen in SOHO; the actual start might be earlier. No source has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is not clearly seen in SOHO and no source has been found for it, so only plane-of-sky measurement is possible.

note: This CME is visible to the south/southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery, and is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to a data gap from ~2025-03-03T11:24Z to 2025-03-03T17:12Z. The source may be related to a large southwest filament eruption spanning S55W15 to S40W60 seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery starting around 2025-03-03T11:28Z. An associated dimming region is visible in SDO AIA 193 around this time centered near ~S60W20. Due to the data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery at this time, it is difficult to confirm with a triangulated measurement if this event is related to the filament eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2
A plane-of-sky measurement was made using STEREO A COR2 imagery and a longitude of -60 degrees due to a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery at this time.

note: Faint CME first seen in the SSE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-03T17:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a date gap 03/14:23Z to 03/21:38Z. The source of this event may be related to faint field line movement visible over the S/SE limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery starting around 2025-03-03T17:00Z

cmeAnalyses.note: Low confidence plane-of-sky measurement based on best fit in limited frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3

note: Faint CME visible to the S/SE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source of this CME is a filament eruption centered near S27E45 (below active regions 14012 and 14011) starting around 2025-03-04T03:20Z as seen in SDO/AIA 304. Associated moving/opening field lines and possible EUV wave visible to the south and south west towards the south pole as seen in SDO/AIA 193 indicating southern deflection, likely due to the coronal hole located N/NE of the source location. Associated brightening and dimming are also visible in SDO/AIA 131, 304, and 193 in the area of the source with additional dimming visible further south closer to the south pole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of faint front in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME partially overlaps the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2025-03-04T03:48Z. The potential source for this CME is a filament eruption near S42W95 with associated moving/opening field lines visible along the SW limb in SDO/AIA 304 and 171 starting around 2025-03-04T03:51Z. There appears to be southward deflection possibly due to coronal holes in the vicinity of the source location. The coronal holes and the eruptions deflection are more clearly seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of the CME using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Strong deflection is likely due to nearby coronal holes.

note: Faint CME with diffuse front visible along streamer to the south in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around S25E42 (below ARs 14012 and 14011) visible in SDO/AIA 304 starting around 2025-03-04T09:30Z. Brightening and dimming are also visible in SDO/AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This event is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The source is likely an eruption visible on/near the southwest limb starting around 2025-03-04T18:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement with more SOHO LASCO C3 frames now available. Based on the approximate source location.
Preliminary measurement based on the approximate source location.

note: This CME is visible to the west/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-03-04T19:38Z. The source is likely related to an eruption visible near the northwest limb (centered near ~N15W80) starting around 2025-03-04T21:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: A faint CME with a fuzzy front to the northeast, closely followed by a second, brighter, front, better seen in SOHO than in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. There is a super faint wider front that might indicate a shock front. No source has been found for this CME, so it is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The front is very unclear/fuzzy in STEREO A COR2 and no source has been found for this event, so this analysis is very uncertain.

note: Very faint flux rope CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, then seen as an extremely faint feature to the SE in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a set of loops/flux rope seen lifting off from on or just beyond the southeast limb (loop spans approx. S20-S25 and E110-E90) starting at about 2025-03-05T03:34Z in SDO AIA 171 imagery. Post-eruptive arcades appear several hours later and seemingly from the same location starting at about 2025-03-05T06:36Z in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using the location of the source seen in UV imagery of the Earth-facing disk and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The full leading edge and a small interior flux rope are both faintly visible in C2, but this CME is only tentatively seen as an extremely faint feature for two frames in STEREO A COR2, so there is some uncertainty with this measurement. The best fit parameters match well with the approximated source location if taking into account some southern deflection, though, which increases confidence a bit. Leading edge is too diffuse to track in SOHO LASCO C3.
Plane-of-sky measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. Leading edge is too diffuse to track in SOHO LASCO C3.

note: CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and briefly in STEREO COR2A before a data gap begins at 2025-03-05T11:53Z. The source is a small filament which spanned roughly N28W55->N28W70 (centered N28W62) near AR 14006 (N18W70) at 2025-03-05T10:09Z just before erupting. The eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 304 as the filament material brightening and lifting off, and also observed in SDO AIA 171 as field line movement to the NW.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement using mostly SOHO LASCO C2/C3 frames, with two STEREO COR2A frames helping triangulate the longitude prior to its data gap beginning at 2025-03-05T11:53Z. This CME front diffuses out after an initial solid view in LASCO C2, it was much easier to track the leading edge in the earliest frames used for this measurement.

note: A CME seen north in both coronagraphs and following the path of the 2025-03-05T11:00Z CME.  Its likely source is a minor eruption with minor dimming and jagged ejecta seen in the NE at 2025-03-05T18:18Z in AIA 171 (N32W55), followed by the minor post-eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs. There seems to be a northward and eastward deflection from the location of the source eruption.

note: Narrow and faint jet CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Source is a faint and narrow loop / opening field line movement can be seen in GOES SUVI 284 off the NE limb, first distinguishable at 2025-03-06T03:00Z when the loop is already near the edge of the SUVI 284 field of view. There are two candidates for the origin of this loop: 1) a very small instance of brightening at 2025-03-06T02:58Z from AR 4017 (S05E56), or 2) from just beyond the NE limb, likely located near the northernmost footpoint of the arc of field lines visible on the NE limb in UV imagery which turns into the streamer visible to the NE in coronagraph imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2. Narrow leading edge is faint but well-defined in C2, distinguishable but not as well-defined in STEREO A COR2, and defined for only two frames in C3.

note: Faint loop CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Source is an area of dimming and opening field lines seen from AR 4016 (S26E33) and the surrounding area, which spans from S10 to S30 and E30 to E40, starting at 2025-03-06T04:39Z in SDO AIA 193. The opening field lines appear to be deflected southward and westward in SDO AIA 193/171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Leading edge is too diffuse to reliably track in SOHO LASCO C3. This best-fit measurement corroborates the southward and westward deflection of this eruption from the source location as was suspected based on visual inspection of UV imagery.

note: Bright CME first seen to the SSE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-07T02:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event in an eruption centered at approx. S30E10 beginning at approx. 07/01:15Z as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Dimming is also visible in SDO AIA 193 exhibiting a strong Southern deflection. A larger coronal hole is visible to the North of this eruption sight in SDO AIA 211, which may be contributing to the Southern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-07T02:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen in the SW by SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 07/01:28Z centered at approx. S40W90 with Southern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Faint CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-07T03:12Z. This CME fades before exiting the FOV in C2 and is therefore not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 or STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is a minor eruption seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 304 beginning at approx. 07/02:45Z, along with faint field line opening seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to source location near the limb and lack of reliable STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-07T09:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is some minor field line movement seen along the Eastern limb in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2. The source of this event is an area of field line opening seen along or just beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284. Post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 94 and 131 following the opening. This CME is almost entirely obstructed by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 which lasted from 2025-03-07T14:53Z to 2025-03-07T21:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement tracking the northernmost feature (as seen in SOHO LASCO C2), which seems to correspond to an extremely faint loop seen in late frames of STEREO A COR2. This feature in C2 appears to be traveling slightly faster than the surrounding/overlapping material, which becomes diffuse and seems to fall apart or loose momentum before reaching the edge of the C2 field of view. The northernmost feature reaches into the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: CME seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and in later STEREO A COR2 frames. Source is a filament close to the SW limb (spans S35W60 to S30W90) seen lifting off starting at 2025-03-07T18:45Z in SDO AIA 171, 193, and 304. Bright ejecta can be seen off the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 and 304, and in GOES SUVI 304 a large loop of ejected filamentary material can be seen by 2025-03-07T19:20Z, which fully departs the GOES SUVI field of view by about 2025-03-07T20:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Loop CME seen to the SW in both SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Source is an M1.6 flare and eruption from AR 4016 (S26E10). Dimming with southward deflection is seen starting at 2025-03-07T20:59Z in SDO AIA 193 and spans about 10 degrees radially around AR 4016 i.e. from S15 to S35 and from E20 to E00. Opening field lines with some southward deflection can be seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 as well. Post-eruptive brightening can be seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304, including some from nearby AR 4012 (S13W06) starting at 2025-03-07T21:04Z. An EUV wave is seen propagating southward from AR 4016 in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between the abundance of SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 frames available. Source location with southern deflection observed in UV imagery was taken into consideration when conducting this measurement.

note: This narrow on-disk CME is seen as a faint flux rope due south in SOHO LASCO C2 and simultaneously as a faint loop to the southeast in STEREO A COR2, which is currently 30 degrees to the west of SOHO LASCO. The source is a subtle eruption from AR 4012 (S20W00) starting at 2025-03-07T21:35Z, seen as dimming, brightening, and field line opening in SDO AIA 193 and 171, as well as GOES SUVI 284 and 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of STEREO A COR2, four frames of SOHO LASCO C3, and two frames of SOHO LASCO C2. The leading edge is very faint in SOHO LASCO imagery; it is much more well-defined in STEREO A COR2. This CME visually overlaps with CME:2025-03-07T21:49Z in both SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2.

note: Relatively slow, diffuse CME seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2. Source is an eruption seen close to the SW limb as evidenced by moving field lines seen lifting off starting as early as 2025-03-08T06:08Z best in GOES SUVI 284. The signature is also seen well by opening magnetic field lines in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge of the southwest portion of the CME and not the leading edge seen more to the south in STEREO A COR2 later frames.

note: Narrow and fast CME seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery associated with a point source eruption from Active Region 14011 (S14W29) seen erupting around 2025-03-08T14:45Z in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 284. The active region footpoint is seen to have a small brightening during the eruption followed by a dark jet of plasma material leaving to the southwest with some deflection to the west.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using only SOHO C2 as the CME is not seen well in STEREO A, possibly being edge on. This measurement assumes some modest deflection of a few degrees to the west.

note: Faint, narrow, somewhat asymmetrical CME to the northeast, with a protruding pointy nose. Source: minor eruption/prominence on/behind the northeast limb seen in SDO AIA 304 at 2025-03-08T22:10Z and as very minor movement of field lines behind the NE limb in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: At the time of analysis no STEREO A COR2 imagery is available because of the nighttime data gap. The source is likely behind the NE limb (possibly on the limb). No definitive 3D analysis is possible at the time, so only plane-of-sky measurement is performed.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-03-09T11:53Z. The source is likely related to an eruption, which exhibits northern deflection, visible on or slightly beyond the northeast limb (~N30E90) starting around 2025-03-03T12:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the approximate source location.

note: This event is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and south in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from Active Region 14012 (S15W40) starting around 2025-03-10T03:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. The source eruption exhibits a southeast deflection, suggesting that the CME parameters may measure southeast of the on-disk source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location, accounting for southeast deflection, and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs.

note: This event is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption visible on or slightly beyond the northeast limb starting around 2025-03-10T05:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the south in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a minor eruption near Active Region 14016 (~S25W25) starting around 2025-03-10T08:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. Dimming is observed in SDO AIA 193 at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location, accounting for southern deflection, and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is faint but visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is too faint to observe in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field-line movement visible over the southwest limb starting around 2025-03-10T10:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees. A triangulated measurement was not available as this CME is undetectable in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is faint but visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery before the leading edge becomes too diffuse to observe. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint and relatively narrow CME to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. The leading edge appears slightly brighter in STEREO A COR2 than in SOHO LASCO. The source is opening field lines seen starting at 2025-03-11T03:35Z located on or just beyond the W limb as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 (W120-130 from SDO AIA perspective) and spanning approximately N00 to S10 in latitude, although the eruption likely extends to farther beyond the limb. Field line movement and the disappearance of a small loop of material can be seen from the same location in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery between the 2025-03-11T03:45Z and 2025-03-11T04:45Z frames.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in UV imagery and best fit between a few frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery. The leading edge is very faint in both coronagraphs and becomes too diffuse to reliably track about halfway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: Super narrow jet (with the 2 degree half-width or so), seen only in SOHO LASCO C2 and faintly in a few early timestamps of C3. Not discernible in STEREO A COR2, likely because of its faintness. Likely associated with the M1.1 flare from AR 14024 (N5W47).

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis as this jet was measured with the 10 deg halfwidth using the one-coronagraph method in swpc_cat, based only on SOHO imagery and on the location of the associated flare. While the jet is extremely narrow (<2 degrees half-width, lowest half-width setting in swpc_cat that we have to use is 10 degrees).

note: Narrow, relatively fast CME seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and more directed towards the north in STEREO Ahead COR2 imagery composed of a fainter, faster shock. No sources on the Earth-facing disk in EUV imagery seem to be associated with this event, so the CME is likely associated with far-sided eruptive activity.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using triangulation from two spacecraft (SOHO, STEREO A) to determine a potential longitude; approximately a 20 degree uncertainty in longitude.

note: Narrow CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 during a COR2A data gap. Appears to be associated with a minor eruption from Active Region 14024 (N07W57) and C9.6-class flare as evidenced by dimming seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 294 starting around 2025-03-11T21:28Z as well as brightening visible in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using only SOHO imagery and knowledge of the source eruption location to determine the longitude.

note: Narrow, relatively fast CME seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap; it appears similar in appearance to the CME: 2025-03-11T18:24Z which was determined to likely be far-sided. Few, if any sources on the Earth-facing disk suggest that this CME occurs with eruptive activity on the Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO plane of sky measurement as STEREO A COR2 data is not available at the time of the eruption.

note: Bulbous jet-like CME to northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the north in STEREO, similar to the 2025-03-11T23:24Z CME. No clear source was found on disk but there are some movements of field lines behind the limb in the NE after 05Z in AIA 193. The CME is likely farsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based solely on the fit with two coronagraphs.

note: A super faint jet to the northwest, seen mostly in SOHO LASCO C2 and in a few early timestamps of C3 and too faint to be seen in STEREO A COR2. There is no flare that can be associated with it but there is some brightening in AR 14024 after 2025-03-12T06Z seen in SDO AIA 193 and it is possibly associated with activity in this Active Region.

cmeAnalyses.note: No clear source found on disk and no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this faint event, so only plane-of-sky measurement is definitive.

note: Super faint and narrow jet only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery and in a few early C3 images and not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source has been found for this jet.

cmeAnalyses.note: Super faint and narrow jet only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery and in a few early C3 images and not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source has been found for this jet.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 white light imagery starting at 2025-03-12T20:04Z. Also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2. This jet may have been visible in running difference imagery shortly before it was visible in white light imagery and has a half-width of less than ten degrees. There is not a good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk; however, there are some possible post eruptive arcades on or just beyond the NE limb (approximately N35-N40) best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2025-03-12T21:15Z that could be related to this jet.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3. A plane-of-sky measurement was chosen due to the lack of certainty in a source location.

note: Faint CME seen to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source may be field line movement in SDO AIA 171 observed over the SSW limb beginning around 2025-03-12T23:18Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Difficult to triangulate measurement between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A due to the faint, wispy nature of the leading edge. Good confidence in the high southern latitude and longitude around W50-W60.

note: Faint CME seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO COR2A for a few frames before it fades, never reaching LASCO C3 imagery. First seen more clearly in SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery at 2025-03-13T03:48Z. The source for this CME is likely field line movement in SDO AIA 171 on or just inside the SE limb starting around 2025-03-13T02:53Z, from the northern side of AR 14028.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO COR2A, using only the earliest frames as the CME fades into the running difference background by 2025-03-13T06:00Z.

note: CME seen to the SW in STEREO COR2A only, as SOHO LASCO C2/C3 is in a data gap from 2025-03-13T07:30Z -> 2025-03-13T22:10Z. No source for this CME is observed in SDO AIA or STEREO A EUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky measurement as no SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery is available. At the CME start time STEREO A is located 30.981 degrees west of Earth, putting its western plane-of-sky around W121 relative to Earth.

note: CME seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 composed of a bright narrow bulk and a fainter shock extending to the north and west relative to the bulk. The source is a minor eruption from near Active Region 4020 (N20E13) with northern deflection as seen in SDO AIA 193, 171, 304 as early as 2025-03-13T16:49Z; darkening in SDO AIA 193, brightening in SDO AIA 304 and the appearance of a breaking loop in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: One spacecraft measurement (SOHO) of the leading edge assuming some modest northern deflection and fitting relative to the source observed in EUV imagery.

Measurement of wider shock front using only SOHO C2 and knowledge of the source as determined from EUV imagery. Attached WSA-Enlil+Cone simulation was executed in support of SEP models and should not be used for CME trajectory analysis. Based on simulation output, there is low confidence the CME may arrive at Earth very weakly.

note: CME seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and east-northeast in STEREO A COR2A composed of a bright narrow bulk extending to the northeast and second more minor outflow seen more to the north. The source may be associated with a minor eruption seen near the eastern limb around E80 as early as 2025-03-14T02:00Z; mostly in GOES SUVI 284 imagery, or the eruption may be far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft leading edge measurement in order to triangulate a possible longitude; uncertainty in longitude up to +/- 20 degrees.

note: CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-14T15:25Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 14/15:53Z. The source of this event is a minor eruption from AR 4022 (N08E11) beginning at approx. 14/14:28Z. Dimming seen in SDO AIA 193 and 211 suggest a strong Eastern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. This event is measuring slightly more narrow than the SWPC_CAT lower limit of 10 degrees.

note: Complex-shaped, somewhat pointy-nosed and possibly partial halo CME to the southwest, seen the brightest in STEREO A COR2. The much fainter shock can be best seen mostly as it pushes the streamer in the south south west towards the east. Likely deflection of about 10 to 20 degrees eastward relative to the source at W125 caused by a large coronal hole located to the northwest of Active Region 4012.
